name: Barn Swallow
facts: Barn Swallows are aerial insect hunters, swooping low over fields and water to catch flies and mosquitoes on the wing.
They build cup-shaped mud nests on barns, bridges, and porches, often returning to the same areas year after year.
Their forked tails and swift, acrobatic flight make them one of the most recognizable summer birds in the Midwest.
